About me

I’m a first-year mechanical engineering student at Duke from New Jersey. I got interested in engineering as a kid, watching space and NASA videos while dreaming of becoming an astronaut. Later, watching Formula 1, I realized I was just as curious about the hands-on side: the mechanical systems and design that make these machines work. That curiosity led me to mechanical engineering and aerospace.

My Interests

Research and design opportunities in mechanical design, aerospace and robotics, where I can keep building and testing real prototypes. I’m especially interested in hands-on projects where I can deepen core engineering skills, such as CAD modeling, simulation and programming.

Pediatric ankle-foot orthoses

2026 to present. Research and lead designer, with Duke University School of Medicine.

Problem

Children who need ankle-foot orthoses in Peru often can’t get braces that fit as they grow. Traditional casting and fabrication are slow and costly.

Design process

I model the brace parametrically in Onshape so one design adapts to different leg sizes. Each child’s anatomy is sculpted as a mesh in Blender to guide the fit.

Current prototype

A ventilated shell reduces weight, hook-and-loop straps at the calf and ankle allow adjustment, and a soft footbed layer sits against the foot.

Next

Clinical review with the Duke School of Medicine team, then iteration on fit and material. Add your test results here.

PID control for differential-drive robots

2025. NJ Governor’s School of Engineering and Technology at Rutgers, supported by Lockheed Martin.

GitHub repositoryPaper (IEEE Xplore)

Standard PID controllers struggle on differential-drive robots because linear and angular motion are coupled. We added a moving integral window, a target yaw tied to linear speed, and removal of saturated errors from the integral. The robot now corrects position first, then rotates in place.

u(t) = Kpe(t) + Ki ∫ e(t) dt + Kd de(t)dt
The standard PID equation: u(t) is the controller output, e is the error, and Kp, Ki and Kd are the proportional, integral and derivative gains. Our version computes the integral term over a moving window of recent errors only.
p ≈ 1.3×10⁻¹³Enhanced PID travels less than the base controller (n = 30, α = 0.01)
p ≈ 7.5×10⁻⁹A* generates paths faster than Dijkstra on 26-node maps, with identical paths
+41.8% / +169.3%Larger x and y errors for the tuned P controller in GazeboSim

Assistive audio-identification device

2026 to present. Developer.

I conceived, designed and built this prototype independently. RFID tags on objects trigger an Arduino-based reader that announces what they are, helping visually impaired users move through everyday spaces. Professor Shendell (NJ Safe Schools Program) and Dr. Jackson (AJA Greener Futures) support exploring a patent and manufacturing.
